why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 P3), `declined`/`absent` -> `divergence`: the name EXISTS (issue 2027) and correlates `systematic` under `rule:no-shared-ptr`, so `absent` was false -- found by the new `misdeclared_absences` check. It is a NAME COLLISION, not a port: ours is `execute(goal_id)`, the goal-id-keyed form of `ServerGoalHandle::execute()` (ACCEPTED -> EXECUTING); upstream's is the executor-internal `Waitable::execute(std::shared_ptr<void>&)`, which a user program does not call, and which stays unported because the executor owns readiness and entities are arena-registered at creation (RFC-0002). A ported call of upstream's member does not compile (different parameter). PRIOR ROW: phase-417 stage 0 — visible only because the rclcpp adapter (then `rclcpp_compat.hpp`; deleted at stage 6 step A, each declaration moved to the header owning its concept) became a translation unit (issue 1020). The shim ships this TYPE as a name, so its members stop inheriting "we do not have this type" and become their own claim. Not a new gap: a gap INSIDE a type we ship is a different statement from one about a type we do not. `rclcpp_action::Server`'s member surface is the wait-set/`Waitable` protocol (`execute`, `is_ready`, `set_on_ready_callback`) plus `make_shared`; the executor owns readiness here and entities are arena-registered at creation (RFC-0002), so there is nothing for a caller to poll or construct.

issue 2027 (2026-10-24) -- NAME COLLISION, not a port: `rclcpp_action::Server<A>::execute(goal_id)` now exists and is NOT upstream's `Waitable::execute(std::shared_ptr<void>&)`. It is the goal-id-keyed form of `ServerGoalHandle::execute()` (ACCEPTED -> EXECUTING, status published), which upstream keeps on the handle. The `Waitable` member stays absent for the reason above, and a ported call of it does not compile (different parameter).
